questions.q: In a StoryBrand story, who should be cast as the hero?
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a brand's story needs a hero, and that hero must be the customer rather than the company.

questions.q: What role should a customer's problems play in your brand story?
a: The villain the customer must defeat
The setting the story happens in
The reward waiting at the end
The narrator who guides the customer
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends turning the problems customers face into villains that they, as the hero, can vanquish with your product.

questions.q: According to the summary, how many customer desires should a brand story focus on?
questions.why: Lesson 1 stresses focusing on only one of the customer's desires, since a scattered message makes the story unclear.

questions.q: Which three desires does the summary say a vision of transformation should appeal to?
questions.why: Lesson 3 names status, completeness and self-acceptance as the desires that make a happy ending compelling.

questions.q: What did the luxury resort finally realize its customers most wanted?
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the resort simplifying its website once it understood that relaxation was the one desire it needed to serve.
